subject: Engineering Fundamentals
title: Safety Factors: Engineering for the Unexpected
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on Safety Factors: Engineering for the Unexpected.

hook.text: A bridge designed to hold 10 tons is actually built to hold 30. The extra is called the safety factor.

buildup.text: Safety factors account for uncertainties: material defects, construction errors, loads heavier than expected.

discovery.text: Most bridges use a safety factor of 2 to 3. The structure can handle double or triple its rated load.

twist.text: Space engineers use safety factors close to 1.2 because weight is so costly. Every gram counts in orbit.

climax.text: Higher safety factors cost more material and money. Lower ones risk catastrophe. Engineering is a balance.

punchline.text: Build it strong enough. Then triple it.

quiz.question: What does a safety factor of 3 mean for a bridge?
options: The bridge has three backup systems in case one fails
The bridge can handle three times its rated maximum load
The bridge was inspected three times before opening
